I will keep it simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the safest path for me is the usual wheat-maize rotation, because the land, weather, water, and my own experience all fit that system best. I am 53, and with only primary schooling, I do not want to gamble on complicated cash crops that need harder market timing or finer technical management. I want grain that I understand, inputs I can judge, and work I can organize by habit.

So I will grow winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I will use improved or hybrid seed, not old saved seed, because I care more about stable yield and fewer problems than saving a little money upfront. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, one or two topdressings depending on crop color and growth, two to three irrigations if water allows, and disease control mainly around the key stages. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize to catch the season. For maize, I will apply enough nitrogen for strong growth, keep phosphorus and potassium moderate, irrigate only when the field is truly dry, and spray mainly when pests or disease pressure show up. I will still till the land with rotary tillage because it is what I know, it is practical for my conditions, and it helps me handle wheat stubble and prepare a decent seedbed without making the job too heavy.
